messages:
alex: heads-up: noticed a canary perf regression after the hotfix merge (commit 7f3a9b2). short-sequence p95 on decode jumped ~2.4x vs baseline. metrics in the canary dashboard.
sophie: ugh. which workload / config? shortseq only?
alex: internal shortseq-reply workload (len<=32). bucketed by model and route — only the fused-attn path shows the spike.
jb: timeline? which merge introduced this?
alex: merged 7f3a9b2 about 30m before canary run. PR was #4126, fused-op reorder for attention matmul.
triage-bot: CI perf job `decode-p95-shortseq` failed on canary: +145% p95 vs baseline (CI run 2026-03-18T09:04Z).
ci-bot: perf regression detected: job=decode-p95-shortseq, delta=+145%, threshold=+20%. See: https://ci.redwood.example/perf/4126/compare
mike: can you paste a flame of the hot canary?
alex: attaching profiler snippet (condensed).
```
# cpu flame (top stacks):
1) fused_attn::dispatch_kernel
2) decode::kv_prefetch_wait
3) cuda_memcpy_async (spike)
4) matmul::small_batch_path
```

sophie: interesting: `kv_prefetch_wait` shows more time than before. could be scheduling/order change causing more memcopy stalls for short sequences.
jb: i can repro locally with `./run_perf --profile --model=v1 --seq=16 --batch=4`. command: `scripts/repro.sh 7f3a9b2 --shortseq`
alex: repro works here too. I see a ~2x increase in memcpy stalls when fused-attn reorder is enabled.
mike: quick guess: kernel selector is choosing a different matmul kernel that forces synchronous memcpy or disables an async path for small batches.
sophie: check kernel selection table for matmul slot at runtime: `TRACE=kernel:selector DEBUG=1`
alex: ran trace, snippet: `selector: matmul->kernel_small_gemm_v2 (priority 40) (prefetch=false)` — before merge it picked `kernel_small_gemm_v1 (prefetch=true)`.
jb: so reorder changed the ordering of fused ops which altered the memory pattern; kernel selector heuristics now pick v2 because it appears cheaper in isolation. but v2 disables overlapping memcpy.
sophie: this is terrifyingly subtle. options: revert the PR, adjust selector heuristics to prefer prefetch-enabled kernels for shortseq patterns, or update fused reorder to preserve mem patterns.
mike: let's bisect to be sure it's PR 7f3a9b2. can someone trigger a quick bisect? it was a small changeset so bisect is fast.
alex: starting bisect now (local). will update with commit that flips perf back.
(20m later)
alex: bisect result: regression introduced by 7f3a9b2 (no other commits in between). reproducer comparison attached.
jeff: (from infra) can we hold the rollout?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused for service `inference-runtime` (canary-id c-2026-03-18-09-spot). Pause triggered by perf-alert rule `canary-p95-spike`.
ci-bot: created issue perf/4126-regression and added regression label. link: https://issues.redwood.example/4126-regression
sophie: proposed short-term mitigation: disable fused-op reorder flag for canary/dedicated until we ship a selector patch. we can flip a dynamic flag via rollout config.
mike: I'd prefer revert of the PR if it's blocking production rollouts. Is revert small?
jb: revert PR is tiny (revert of #4126), I'll open it now as #4130.
jb: PR #4130 opened -> https://git.redwood/PR/4130 (revert 7f3a9b2).
alex: testing revert locally now.
(10m later)
alex: revert restores baseline p95 locally. canary metrics show p95 back within 3% of baseline after revert merge.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout resumed and completed for `inference-runtime`.
triage-bot: regression resolved: job=decode-p95-shortseq delta=+2.9% (within threshold).
sophie: follow-up: create a unit test that validates kernel selector chooses prefetch-enabled kernels when fused-reorder present for shortseq shapes. also add perf test to CI for the shortseq case.
mike: and a long-term fix: update kernel selector cost model to account for overlapped memcpy benefit and fused-op ordering.
jb: noted. I'll keep #4130 open until we have selector patch PR. assigning to @sophie and @mike for follow-ups.
alex: thanks everyone. good catch.
(references)
- revert PR: https://git.redwood/PR/4130
- original PR: https://git.redwood/PR/4126
- perf CI: https://ci.redwood.example/perf/4126/compare
- issue: https://issues.redwood.example/4126-regression
